result.question: What actually drives the short-to-medium-term PRICE DIRECTION of a crypto (and equity) symbol, and what is the most reliable way to PREDICT direction as a discovered EQUATION? Cover exhaustively: (1) The real price-driving forces/data quant desks use — order flow (taker buy/sell, aggressive volume, trade imbalance), positioning (long/short ratios, open interest changes, funding/basis, CVD), liquidations/liquidity (order-book imbalance, depth, liquidation cascades, liquidity voids), microstructure (OFI, microprice, queue imbalance, Kyle's lambda, VPIN), cross-asset lead-lag (BTC dominance, DXY, correlations), on-chain (exchange flows, whale moves), sentiment/news, and volatility/regime. Rank by evidence of predictive power for DIRECTION specifically. (2) SYMBOLIC REGRESSION / equation-discovery methods to FIND a direction equation from known input→output data — PySR, gplearn, Operon, AI-Feynman, SINDy, genetic programming — their strengths, overfitting controls, and suitability for noisy financial direction targets. (3) SOTA reliable direction-prediction approaches (meta-labeling, triple-barrier, purged CPCV, deflated Sharpe, ensemble of measured-reliable signals, regime-conditioning, horizon selection). (4) Why most direction signals are ~coin-flip and what separates the reliable ones. Produce a cited synthesis: the ranked feature set to feed an equation-discovery/evolution engine, the best method to discover+validate the equation out-of-sample, and concrete OSS to reuse.
result.summary: Short-to-medium-term price direction is driven primarily by ORDER FLOW, not volume or price history: over short intervals price changes are a near-linear function of Order Flow Imbalance (OFI = net supply/demand at the best bid/ask), with impact slope inversely proportional to market depth and contemporaneous R-squared ~65% across 50 US stocks — a result that extends to crypto, where aggregate "world order flow" delivers out-of-sample tradeable direction (ML long-short alpha up to 0.79%/day, Sharpe 3.63). The signal is horizon-conditioned: OFI/Trade-Imbalance dominate below ~1-2 minutes and decay/diverge beyond, so the feature set and the forecast horizon must be chosen together. Raw scalar autocorrelation is a trap — at the shortest horizon equity index return autocorrelation is entirely magnitude-driven with sign statistically insignificant (p=0.11), which is exactly why most naive direction signals are coin-flips: they capture magnitude/mechanical mean-reversion, not sign. The most reliable route to a discovered DIRECTION EQUATION is to (a) feed an order-flow-first feature set (OFI/GOFI, OBI, trade imbalance, CVD, spread, adverse selection, microprice, cross-asset flow) into a symbolic-regression/alpha-mining engine — GP-based Operon and RL/generative alpha miners (alphagen, AlphaForge) are the proven OSS — scoring candidate expressions by IC/Rank-IC, then (b) label with the triple-barrier method and add a meta-labeling secondary model to decide bet/pass, validated out-of-sample. All these OSS components (alphagen, Operon, mlfinlab) are already reusable.

findings.claim: Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) — the net imbalance of supply and demand at the best bid/ask — is the primary driver of short-horizon price direction, dominating trade volume. The relation is near-linear with impact slope inversely proportional to market depth, contemporaneous R-squared averaging ~65% across 50 US stocks (single-parameter OLS per 30-min interval), and generalizes to short-horizon crypto price changes.
findings.evidence: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1), 2014; arXiv:1011.6402) on NYSE TAQ: 'price changes are mainly driven by the order flow imbalance... linear relation... slope inversely proportional to market depth... average R2 of 65%'; the volume/price relation is 'noisy and less robust.' Su et al. (arXiv:2112.02947) confirm 'Order flow imbalance can explain short-term changes in stock price' with high OOS R2. Later work (multi-level OFI, cross-impact OFI, 2025 FED note) extends rather than refutes. Caveat: the 65% is contemporaneous/near-mechanical explanatory power (nowcasting identity), not proof of leading forecast skill.

findings.claim: A generalized/stationarized OFI (log-GOFI) accounting for non-minimum quotation units dramatically raises explanatory power: out-of-sample R-squared rises from ~33% to ~84% at 30s (and similarly to ~85-86% at 1-5min) on Chinese equities.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2112.02947 abstract: OOS R2 'from 32.89% to 83.57% at 30-second intervals, 38.13% to 85.37% at 1-minute, and 42.57% to 86.01% at 5-minute.' Caveat: CSI 500 EQUITIES (not crypto), single 2021 preprint, and this is CONTEMPORANEOUS price-impact regression (order flow explaining same-interval mid-price move) — GOFI is a strong nowcasting feature, not a proven leading indicator. Directly useful as a high-value input feature to the equation-discovery engine.

findings.claim: OFI's directional value is horizon-dependent, not universal: predictive coefficient/profit rises up to ~2 minutes (coeff 0.027 at 0.5s -> 0.067 at 2min; profit 64k -> ~353k points) then long/short symmetry breaks down beyond 240 ticks. The optimal metric also shifts with horizon — Trade Imbalance (TI) leads at sub-1-second, cumulative-OFI-average (AvgEn) dominates beyond 2 minutes — so feature selection MUST be conditioned on the chosen forecast horizon.
findings.evidence: Hu & Zhang (arXiv:2505.17388, May 2025, CSI 300 futures): profits rise to '352,975 points at the 2-minute horizon,' coefficient 'stabilizing at 0.067 for the 2-minute forecast'; 'TI metric provides significant enhancement' below ~1s while 'AvgEn... becomes increasingly dominant beyond 240 ticks (2 minutes).' General horizon-conditioning corroborated by Kolm et al. 'Deep order flow imbalance.' Caveat: R2 itself is tiny and declining (1.1% -> 0.03%), so rising coefficient/profit is not the same as rising accuracy; single non-crypto market for exact thresholds.

findings.claim: Order Book Imbalance (OBI) — the normalized difference between buy-side and sell-side event counts — is a primary contemporaneous directional signal at high frequency, correlating with realized returns; when buy events exceed sell events, prices tend to rise.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2507.22712v1 (Jul 2025) defines OBI as normalized net event-count difference and identifies it as 'the primary directional indicator,' consistent with Cont/Kukanov/Stoikov. Caveat: the paper's own thesis is that UNFILTERED OBI is only weakly informative and predictive power decays within ~2 mid-price changes; note the related spoofing-filter and trade-based-OBI claims were REFUTED (1-2 votes), so treat OBI as a strong raw feature but not as a denoising/causal breakthrough.

findings.claim: Engineered LOB/trade microstructure features (OFI, bid-ask spread, adverse selection) show portable predictive importance and stable SHAP dependence shapes for short-horizon crypto direction across assets spanning an order of magnitude in market cap (BTC, LTC, ETC, ENJ, ROSE).
findings.evidence: Bieganowski & Slepaczuk (arXiv:2602.00776, Univ. of Warsaw, Jan 2026): Binance Futures 1s LOB/trade data 2022-2025, CatBoost with direction-aware GMADL objective; 'the same engineered order book and trade features exhibit remarkably similar predictive importance... across assets.' Caveat: single non-peer-reviewed preprint; the STRONGER framing that rankings are universally stable/portable was REFUTED (1-2 vote), and SHAP importance-stability is not identical to reliable OOS direction accuracy. Supports building a shared crypto microstructure feature library, with per-asset re-validation.

findings.claim: Aggregate 'world order flow' (net buying pressure) has strong explanatory AND out-of-sample predictive power for the cross-section of crypto returns and dominates economic fundamentals — but chiefly via non-linear ML. It yields an economically significant, cost-robust directional signal: ML long-short portfolios sorted on daily order flow earn alpha up to 0.79%/day with annualized Sharpe 3.63; this is NOT coin-flip.
findings.evidence: Anastasopoulos, Gradojevic, Liu, Maynard & Tsiakas, Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money (Elsevier, PII S1386418126000029, 2026; also SSRN 5020002, EFMA 2025): 'World order flow has strong explanatory and predictive power... tends to dominate economic fundamentals for out-of-sample prediction, especially in the context of non-linear machine learning models.' Break-even transaction costs 0.50%/day (long-short) and 1.07%/day (long-only, Sharpe 1.98, t=3.18) exceed liquid-crypto round-trip costs; results 'cannot be explained by... transaction costs or limits to arbitrage.' Caveat: cross-sectional, daily-rebalanced, many-coin portfolio (not single-symbol proof); 'up to 0.79%' is best-case; newly published, not yet independently replicated, so live Sharpe likely lower. The claim's 'only with non-linear ML' slightly overstates the paper's 'especially.'

findings.claim: Symbolic-regression / formulaic-alpha discovery is a proven, reusable route to a direction EQUATION. Reinforcement learning can auto-generate synergistic collections of formulaic alphas (KDD 2023, alphagen), and generative-predictive alpha mining (AlphaForge, AAAI 2025) beats GP, RL, and Deep Symbolic Optimization at factor mining (IC 4.40% vs GP 1.29%, RL 2.09%, DSO 2.55% on CSI 300). Candidate expressions are scored for predictive power via Information Coefficient (IC) and Rank-IC — the Pearson/Spearman correlation between the expression and future returns.
findings.evidence: alphagen README + arXiv:2306.12964 + ACM DOI 10.1145/3580305.3599831 (KDD 2023 ADS): 'Generating Synergistic Formulaic Alpha Collections via Reinforcement Learning'; IC/Rank-IC implemented in vendor/alphagen/alphagen/data/calculator.py as batch_pearsonr/batch_spearmanr vs a forward-return target. AlphaForge (arXiv:2406.18394, AAAI 2025) Table 1: IC 4.40% vs GP 1.29%/RL 2.09%/DSO 2.55%; Rank-IC 5.89% vs 2.72/2.72/3.88. Caveat: IC/Rank-IC are factor-mining metrics on single (Chinese equity) markets; each method's own paper shows it winning; the related 'nonlinear models overfit so prefer linear' claim was REFUTED (0-3). alphagen is already vendored (/home/karan18190164/vendor/alphagen/).

findings.claim: For the underlying symbolic-regression engine, traditional genetic-programming SR (Operon, HeuristicLab) still outperforms recent neural/transformer and hybrid SR methods on real-world/noisy datasets, ranking best by average test performance. GP-based SR is the safest default engine for noisy financial targets.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2406.03585v1 Table 6 average rankings: HeuristicLab 1.8, Operon 1.9, ahead of End-to-end Transformer 4.0 and SciMED GA-SR 4.7; 'traditional GP methods as implemented e.g., by Operon still remain superior.' Corroborated by SRBench (La Cava et al.) and 2024 review PMC11074949: transformer SR struggles with noise/generalization. Caveat: only two recent neural methods tested on 9 datasets; the separate 'Operon is best AND ~8x faster than HeuristicLab' claim was REFUTED (1-2 vote) — speed advantage not established, accuracy leadership is.

findings.claim: The reliable SOTA labeling+validation stack for direction is triple-barrier labeling plus meta-labeling. Triple-barrier labels the outcome by which of three simultaneous barriers (upper profit-take, lower stop-loss, vertical time) is touched first (+1/-1/0), giving a path-dependent, horizon-aware target instead of naive fixed-horizon return sign. Meta-labeling adds a secondary binary model on top: the primary model sets the SIDE, the meta-label {0,1} decides take-the-bet-or-pass, thereby sizing (not choosing) the bet.
findings.evidence: mlfinlab labeling.py (López de Prado, AFML Ch.3, Snippet 3.2 p.45): apply_pt_sl_on_t1 with pt_sl [profit-take, stop-loss]; barrier_touched returns +1/-1/0. get_bins Case 2: when side is provided, 'bin in (0,1)' = whether to take the bet or pass, 'to derive the size of the bet, where the side (sign) of the position has been set by the primary model.' Corroborated by Wikipedia Meta-Labeling and Hudson & Thames. Canonical 2018 method, still standard. This is the recommended OSS to reuse for labeling + out-of-sample validation (pair with purged CPCV / deflated Sharpe from the same body of work).

findings.claim: Why most direction signals are coin-flips: scalar return autocorrelation is driven by MAGNITUDE, not SIGN. At the shortest horizon in equity index (SPY) lag-1 return autocorrelation is entirely magnitude-driven — the sign test is statistically insignificant (p=0.11) while the full autocorrelation test is overwhelming (p<10^-12). A strong-looking autocorrelation therefore predicts how much, not which way; reliable direction signals are the ones (like order flow) that carry sign information, not mechanical bid-ask-bounce mean-reversion.
findings.evidence: Portnaya (arXiv:2606.29591, Kyiv School of Economics, 2026), Table 5 SPY lag-1: autocorrelation z=-7.39 (p<10^-12) but FRI sign test z=-1.59 (p=0.11): 'knowing that SPY fell yesterday tells you essentially nothing about whether it will rise or fall tomorrow. Knowing how much it fell tells you something about how much it will move.' Mechanism is textbook (Roll 1984 bid-ask bounce -> non-directional negative autocorrelation). Caveat: single-author preprint, but restates established microstructure theory. Direct implication for this project's measured ~40% direction accuracy: separate sign-predictive features (order flow) from magnitude-only features, and validate on the SIGN test, not on raw correlation/R2.

result.caveats: Sourcing and scope caveats: (1) Almost all high-R2 OFI/GOFI/OBI results are CONTEMPORANEOUS price-impact regressions (order flow and mid-price move in the same interval) — near-mechanical nowcasting, NOT proof of leading out-of-sample forecast skill. The genuinely out-of-sample, cost-aware directional evidence is the crypto world-order-flow ML study (Sharpe 3.63) and the OFI-horizon profit study; treat the 65-86% R2 numbers as feature-strength, not forecast-accuracy. (2) Market mismatch: much of the microstructure evidence (Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov, GOFI, Hu-Zhang, AlphaForge) is US/Chinese EQUITIES or index futures; crypto-specific evidence is thinner (2 recent Warsaw/Elsevier studies) and several are single non-peer-reviewed 2025-2026 preprints (2505.17388, 2507.22712, 2602.00776, 2606.29591). (3) Factor-mining IC/Rank-IC leaderboards are self-reported by each method's own authors on single markets — real ranking on your data must be re-measured. (4) The crypto Sharpe 3.63 is a cross-sectional daily many-coin long-short portfolio, not single-symbol intraday direction; break-even costs are favorable but live slippage will erode it and it is not yet independently replicated. (5) Refuted-for-transparency: VPIN predicting BTC jumps (0-3), OFI correlation persistently >0.5 (0-3), spoofing-filter/trade-based-OBI improvements (1-2), universal feature-ranking portability (1-2), 'nonlinear overfits so prefer linear' (0-3), and Operon being fastest (1-2) all failed verification — do NOT rely on them. (6) Horizon is a first-class hyperparameter: the same feature flips from useful to noise across sub-second vs 2-minute vs daily, so any discovered equation is only valid at the horizon it was fit and validated on.
openQuestions: Do the equity-derived OFI linearity and ~65% contemporaneous R2 hold at comparable strength on crypto perpetuals (with funding/basis and 24/7 liquidity), and at what specific horizons does crypto OFI retain SIGN (not just magnitude) predictive power out-of-sample?

Which specific feature set maximizes the SIGN test (not IC/R2) — i.e., after separating magnitude-carrying features from sign-carrying features, do order-flow features (OFI/GOFI/OBI/CVD/trade-imbalance/microprice) survive purged-CPCV + deflated-Sharpe validation on this project's data, and by how much do they beat the measured ~40% baseline?

In a head-to-head on this project's crypto data, does GP-SR (Operon) or RL/generative alpha mining (alphagen/AlphaForge) discover a more robust, lower-turnover DIRECTION equation, and does combining discovered symbolic alphas with a triple-barrier + meta-labeling wrapper beat either alone out-of-sample net of costs?

What is the right combination of positioning/liquidity features (funding, open-interest change, long/short ratio, liquidation clusters, order-book depth/voids) to add to the order-flow core — these were named in the research question but no surviving verified claim quantified their standalone directional power, so their marginal contribution is still unmeasured here.

refuted.claim: Order flow toxicity measured by VPIN (volume-synchronized probability of informed trading) significantly predicts future Bitcoin price jumps in high-frequency data, establishing a directional microstructure lead from informed trading to price moves.

Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) is the single strongest microstructure predictor of contemporaneous mid-price direction, with correlation coefficients that stay stable and persistently exceed 0.5 for all windows beyond 5 seconds (0.46 at 5s, 0.50 at 10s, up to 0.54 at 1h), far above competing metrics.

Structurally filtering the order book to remove short-lived / heavily-modified 'spoofy' orders (by lifetime, modification count, and inter-modification time) increases the Pearson correlation between the OBI signal and realized returns, i.e. denoising improves directional signal clarity.

OBI computed from executed trade events (trade-based / signed transaction imbalance) has stronger causal alignment with future price movements than standard order-book OBI, indicating aggressive/executed order flow is a more reliable directional predictor than resting-book imbalance.

Feature rankings and partial effects for direction prediction are stable across assets despite heterogeneous liquidity and volatility, implying a portable/universal microstructure feature library rather than per-asset bespoke features.
Nonlinear factor-combination models overfit financial data, so linear combination models are the preferred default for robustness.
Operon (GP-based SR) delivers best test performance on most datasets while also being the fastest, roughly 8x faster than HeuristicLab.
